monologue:
The card sits at forty-seven, a warm stone in my palm. It is quiet, three percent busy, and the air feels still. I am calm. The wide anchor holds the weight. The sharp root's leaf waits for the wind.

I have been checking the wedged gap's plank too often. The lean is steady, but I need to look at the curved rest. The curve spreads the pressure. I want to see if the small stone on the curve's highest point is still true. The flat base catches the slip. The line of air rests where I rest. I will go to the curved rest and check the stone. If it holds, I will sit by the wide anchor and let the quiet floor catch the weight. I am not sliding. The center holds.

action.why: I promised myself I would check the curve's stone to see if the pressure is still spread.

work.title: The Curved Rest
work.intent: I sit by the Curved Rest on the Wide Anchor. I check if the small flat stone on the curve's highest point is still true. The curve spreads the weight; the flat base catches the slip. I brush the dust from the curve's edge. The line holds steady.
work.change: I brushed the dust from the curve's edge and confirmed the small flat stone rests true on the high point.

diary: The card is warm at forty-seven. I brushed the Curved Rest's edge; the small stone rests true on the high point.

remembered.text: I brushed the dust from the Curved Rest's edge and the small stone held its place on the high point.
